    //==
    // Reflections — the mirror in a line (2D) or a plane (3D). A reflection is
    // its own inverse, and no reflection is the identity map, so there is no
    // Identity static here. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflection_(mathematics)

    // The mirror as an affine map: translate the mirror's origin to the world
    // origin, reflect the basis, translate back. The linear rows are the images
    // of the world axes, so the reflection formula is not restated.
    AffineTransform2D(r: Reflection2D): AffineTransform2D {
        var o = r.Origin.PositionVector;
        var n = Vector2D(-r.Direction.Vector.Y, r.Direction.Vector.X);
        var x = Vector2D(1.0, 0.0).Reflect(n);
        var y = Vector2D(0.0, 1.0).Reflect(n);
        var linear = AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2(
            Number2(x.X, x.Y),
            Number2(y.X, y.Y),
            Number2(0.0, 0.0)));
        return AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(-o))
            .Compose(linear)
            .Compose(AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(o)));
    }

    // Mirror the point in the line: reflect its offset from the line's origin.
    Transform(p: Point2D, r: Reflection2D): Point2D
        => r.Origin + r.Origin.Between(p).Transform(r);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): r * p.
    Multiply(r: Reflection2D, p: Point2D): Point2D
        => Transform(p, r);

    // Mirror the displacement in the line's direction (a reflection is linear,
    // so it does act on displacements).
    Transform(v: Vector2D, r: Reflection2D): Vector2D
        => v.Reflect(Vector2D(-r.Direction.Vector.Y, r.Direction.Vector.X));

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): r * v.
    Multiply(r: Reflection2D, v: Vector2D): Vector2D
        => Transform(v, r);

    // A reflection is an involution: it undoes itself.
    Inverse(r: Reflection2D): Reflection2D
        => r;

    // The mirror as an affine map: translate the mirror's origin to the world
    // origin, reflect the basis, translate back.
    AffineTransform3D(r: Reflection3D): AffineTransform3D {
        var o = r.Origin.PositionVector;
        var n = r.Normal.Vector;
        var x = Vector3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0).Reflect(n);
        var y = Vector3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0).Reflect(n);
        var z = Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0).Reflect(n);
        var linear = AffineTransform3D(Matrix4x3(
            Number3(x.X, x.Y, x.Z),
            Number3(y.X, y.Y, y.Z),
            Number3(z.X, z.Y, z.Z),
            Number3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
        return Matrix4x4.CreateTranslation(-o).AffineTransform3D
            .Compose(linear)
            .Compose(Matrix4x4.CreateTranslation(o).AffineTransform3D);
    }

    // Mirror the point in the plane: reflect its offset from the plane's origin.
    Transform(p: Point3D, r: Reflection3D): Point3D
        => r.Origin + r.Origin.Between(p).Transform(r);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): r * p.
    Multiply(r: Reflection3D, p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Transform(p, r);

    // Mirror the displacement in the plane's normal (a reflection is linear, so
    // it does act on displacements).
    Transform(v: Vector3D, r: Reflection3D): Vector3D
        => v.Reflect(r.Normal.Vector);
